idiom_name: interface port + adapter class + data-class mappers; sealed interface for upstream outcomes
implementation_notes: Kotlin expresses the boundary with an interface port and a plain adapter class, boundary models as data classes, and translation as top-level or extension functions (fun LegacyOrderDto.toDomain(): Order); upstream outcomes that are not exceptions become a sealed interface matched exhaustively, and nullability replaces many optional-field checks. kotlinx.serialization can own the wire half through @SerialName and custom KSerializer, but it does not build the boundary. What replaces the classic class hierarchy is the port interface plus these mapping functions; a heavier facade object is justified when several upstream calls form one domain operation.
pitfalls: Platform types from Java vendor SDKs (String!, List<Foo>!) erase nullability at the seam; declare explicit types and validate before the value enters the domain.
Data classes are shallowly immutable and expose copy(), so a foreign holder of a component collection can still mutate shared state.
Sealed hierarchies are exhaustive only inside their own module (and package); an else branch hides new upstream variants instead of failing the build.
suspend adapters must not block (runBlocking) inside the boundary - that ties up the dispatcher and defeats structured cancellation.
